title: Models and the Foundry catalog · Level 2
slo: Describe language models and use the Foundry catalog to find suitable models.

exercises.question_text: Partner and community models can support experimentation and specialized tasks.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: This would miss a key reason teams may explore these models.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Open-source or vendor-hosted catalog models can support experimentation and specialized tasks.

exercises.explanation: Correct! Partner and community models support broader experimentation, rapid innovation, and specialized work.

exercises.question_text: Reconstruct the statement from the pieces.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The meaning could shift away from adapting an existing model for a need.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Start with fine-tuning, then state that it adapts a pretrained model and explain the purpose.

exercises.correct_answer: Fine-tuning adapts a pretrained model to a particular need
exercises.explanation: The order states the action, what it changes, and the purpose of that change. Fine-tuning adapts an already pretrained model for a particular need.

exercises.question_text: A product manager needs a model with strong Azure integration, preconfigured security, and compliance alignment for a customer-support service. Which model source best fits?

options.rationale: This is correct. Azure-direct models provide strong Azure integration, preconfigured security, and compliance alignment.

options.error_type: Confuses experimentation-oriented models with enterprise Azure integration
options.rationale: These models support experimentation, innovation, and specialized tasks. The requested Azure integration and preconfigured security match Azure-direct models.
options.better_fit: Use partner and community models when open-source or vendor-hosted experimentation suits the need.

feedback.intrinsic: The manager could miss the stated enterprise-focused benefits needed for the service.
feedback.instructional: Match the requirement to the source: Azure-direct models provide the listed integration, security, and compliance features.

options.error_type: Confuses a comparison feature with a model source
options.rationale: A leaderboard ranks models by attributes such as quality, safety, and throughput. It is not a source of models.
options.better_fit: Use a leaderboard to compare candidate models by relevant attributes.

feedback.intrinsic: The manager could compare candidates but would not choose a model source.
feedback.instructional: A leaderboard informs selection; models sold directly by Azure are the source that fits these requirements.

options.error_type: Confuses a prebuilt tool with a model source
options.rationale: Foundry tools are prebuilt capabilities for well-defined use cases. They are not one of the model sources in this comparison.
options.better_fit: Consider a Foundry tool for a well-defined use case needing predictable performance and fast time-to-value.

feedback.intrinsic: The manager would choose a different kind of capability than the requested model source.
feedback.instructional: The question asks which model source fits. Azure-direct models provide the stated enterprise features.

exercises.explanation: Correct! Azure-direct models provide the requested Azure integration, security, and compliance alignment.

exercises.question_text: A developer is selecting a model for a product-description generator and must confirm task fit and safety information. What should the developer inspect in the model entry? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: This is correct. Inference tasks show the work a model supports when generating or processing output.
This is correct. Model cards, constraints, and caveats help assess responsible-use considerations.
This is correct. Model entries typically list capabilities such as text generation, reasoning, coding, multimodal processing, and embeddings.

options.error_type: Confuses model entry information with an agent capability
options.rationale: Working memory is something an agent can maintain during a conversation. It is not listed as information in a model entry.
options.better_fit: Consider working memory when evaluating an agent's conversational behavior.

feedback.intrinsic: The developer would check an agent behavior instead of the model details needed for selection.
feedback.instructional: For task fit and safety information, inspect supported inference tasks, capabilities, and responsible-use documentation.

exercises.explanation: Correct! Those model-entry details show whether the model supports the task and what constraints to consider.

exercises.question_text: Large language models are also called ___.

parts.text: Large language models are also called

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The abbreviation would identify a different category or component.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Use LLM for large language model. SLM means small language model, while an agent and a foundation model mean different things.

exercises.explanation: LLM is the abbreviation for large language model. SLM refers to the smaller model category instead.

exercises.question_text: Arrange the parts to form the correct statement.

feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Name the government workload first, then connect it to the possible need for a domain-specialized model.

exercises.correct_answer: Government workloads may require a domain-specialized model instead
exercises.explanation: This sentence distinguishes specialized government workloads from lightweight phone-app use cases. Such workloads may need a domain-specialized model.

exercises.question_text: A developer is building a customer-support virtual agent that must answer customer questions in natural language. What should provide its core response-generating intelligence?

options.rationale: This is correct. A language model generates the natural-language responses the virtual agent needs.
A catalog helps select models by comparing them. It does not produce customer answers.
options.better_fit: Use the catalog before deployment to discover suitable models.

feedback.intrinsic: The support service would have choices to review but no response generator.
feedback.instructional: Use the catalog to find a model; use the language model to generate answers.

options.error_type: Confuses a workspace with a model
options.rationale: A project is the workspace where Foundry capabilities begin. It does not itself generate natural-language output.
options.better_fit: Create a project to organize Foundry work and client connections.

feedback.intrinsic: The developer would have a workspace but no core responder.
feedback.instructional: A project supports the work around a model; the language model generates responses.

options.error_type: Confuses an evaluation result with a model
options.rationale: A benchmark result reports model performance on standard datasets. It is not a model that can answer a customer.
options.better_fit: Use benchmark results when comparing possible models.

feedback.intrinsic: A score could guide selection, but it could not answer the customer's question.
feedback.instructional: Benchmarks help evaluate models; language models create the requested output.

exercises.explanation: Correct! A language model supplies the natural-language response capability.

exercises.question_text: To use Foundry capabilities, begin by creating a Foundry ___.

parts.text: To use Foundry capabilities, begin by creating a Foundry

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: You would name a feature or component instead of the workspace needed to begin.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Create a Foundry project first. A catalog discovers models, a playground tests them, and an agent is a reusable component.

exercises.explanation: A Foundry project is the workspace for Foundry capabilities and client connections. It is the starting place after obtaining an Azure subscription.

exercises.question_text: A mobile app designer needs AI features in a lightweight phone app. Which choices fit this decision? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: This is correct. An SLM can be a good fit for a lightweight phone application.

options.text: Match the model to the app's needs.
options.rationale: This is correct. Model selection starts with the workload and its constraints.

options.text: Assume a domain-specialized model is required.
options.error_type: Confuses a phone app with a government domain need
options.rationale: A lightweight phone app can be a good SLM use case. Domain specialization is associated with a specialized government application.
options.better_fit: Consider a domain-specialized model for a specialized government workload.

feedback.intrinsic: The designer may add specialization that the lightweight app does not need.
feedback.instructional: Do not assume one model type fits every workload. Start with the app's actual needs.

options.text: Choose a catalog instead of a model.
options.error_type: Confuses a discovery hub with a model choice
options.rationale: The catalog is used to discover and compare models. It is not itself the model selected for the app.
options.better_fit: Use the catalog to locate and compare candidate models.

feedback.intrinsic: The app would still lack a selected model to provide its features.
feedback.instructional: Use the catalog during selection, then choose a model that fits the app.

exercises.explanation: Correct! An SLM is a reasonable choice to consider for a lightweight phone application.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The catalog's role is no longer communicated clearly.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Start with the catalog, state that it is a central hub, then give its purpose.

exercises.correct_answer: The model catalog is a central hub for discovering and using generative AI models
exercises.explanation: The order identifies the catalog first, then explains its discovery purpose. A catalog brings model choices together so they can be found and compared.

exercises.question_text: Mia has an Azure subscription and needs to deploy a customer-support model in Foundry. What should she create first?

options.rationale: This is correct. Using Foundry capabilities begins by creating a Foundry project.

options.error_type: Confuses comparison information with a workspace
options.rationale: A leaderboard ranks models by attributes such as quality, safety, and throughput. It is not the workspace that begins Foundry work.
options.better_fit: Use a leaderboard when comparing candidate models.

feedback.intrinsic: Mia could compare models but would not have the project needed to proceed.
feedback.instructional: A leaderboard supports selection; a Foundry project is the required starting workspace.

options.error_type: Confuses model behavior settings with project setup
options.rationale: Instructions define a model's role, behavior, style, and constraints. They are configured after the workspace is available.
options.better_fit: Write instructions when defining desired model or agent behavior.

feedback.intrinsic: Mia would define behavior before creating the workspace for the deployment.
feedback.instructional: Start with a Foundry project. Instructions shape behavior but do not establish the project.

options.error_type: Confuses evaluation data with project setup
options.rationale: Benchmarks show performance on standard datasets. They do not replace the project needed to use Foundry capabilities.
options.better_fit: Use benchmark information to compare candidate models.

feedback.intrinsic: Evaluation information alone would not create a place to deploy the model.
feedback.instructional: A Foundry project is the workspace needed first; benchmarks help with model evaluation.

exercises.explanation: Correct! Her Azure subscription lets her begin by creating a Foundry project.

exercises.question_text: A developer is choosing a model for a code-generation feature and sees many catalog choices. What can the developer do in the Foundry model catalog? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: This is correct. Capabilities are available catalog filters.
This is correct. Inference tasks can be used to narrow choices.
This is correct. Foundry helps users understand and compare model capabilities.

options.text: Use the catalog as an agent tool.
options.error_type: Confuses model discovery with an agent action tool
options.rationale: The catalog is for discovering, filtering, and comparing models. It is not presented as an action an agent can call.
options.better_fit: Use catalog features when selecting a model before deployment.

feedback.intrinsic: The developer would confuse a selection hub with an action-taking capability.
feedback.instructional: Use the catalog to explore models. Agents can call external actions such as APIs, functions, retrieval, or an MCP server.

exercises.explanation: Correct! The catalog supports filtering and comparing models to find a suitable choice.
